wall_crack.title: Wall crack
wall_crack.why_it_matters: Some cracks are only cosmetic, but wide, long, or growing cracks may indicate movement in the wall or foundation.
possible_causes: Soil settlement or a weak foundation
actions: Mark both ends of the crack with a pencil and the date, then check weekly to see if it grows
Take clear photos with a ruler beside the crack
Keep water away from the wall by fixing gutters and drainage
Do not just plaster over it until the cause is understood
Fill small, stable hairline cracks with a cement-based filler
wall_crack.see_professional: If the crack is wider than about 5 mm, runs diagonally, is near a door or window corner, or keeps growing, ask a registered engineer to inspect.

water_stain.title: Water stain
water_stain.why_it_matters: A stain may indicate a leak or dampness. Ongoing moisture can damage plaster, paint, and timber, and can encourage mold.
possible_causes: Blocked gutters or poor drainage near the wall
actions: Find the source: check the roof above, nearby pipes, and gutters
Fix the leak first, then repair the paint or plaster
Let the wall dry fully before repainting
Open windows to improve airflow
Use anti-fungal paint once the wall is dry
water_stain.see_professional: If the stain keeps coming back, is spreading, or the plaster is falling off, ask a qualified builder or engineer to check.

damaged_roofing.title: Damaged roofing
damaged_roofing.why_it_matters: A damaged roof can let rain in, may weaken the roof structure over time, and can be unsafe in strong wind.
actions: Keep people away from rooms under the damaged area
Do not climb a wet or damaged roof
Cover the opening with a tarpaulin or plastic sheet to stop rain getting in
Replace damaged sheets or tiles and fix loose nails
Clear gutters and trim overhanging branches
damaged_roofing.see_professional: If roof timbers are broken, the roof is sagging, or a ceiling has collapsed, ask a registered engineer or experienced contractor to inspect before repair.

exposed_reinforcement.title: Exposed reinforcement
exposed_reinforcement.why_it_matters: Exposed steel can rust and swell, which cracks the concrete around it and may reduce the strength of that part of the building.
possible_causes: Too little concrete cover over the steel
Water and moisture reaching the steel
actions: Keep people and heavy loads away from the affected area
Do not hang or load anything on that part
Do not just cover it with paint or plaster
Have the damaged concrete assessed before any repair
Keep water away from the area
exposed_reinforcement.see_professional: Always ask a registered engineer to inspect exposed reinforcement, especially in beams, columns, slabs, or balconies.

standing_water.title: Standing water near the building
standing_water.why_it_matters: Water pooling near a building can soak the foundation and walls, cause dampness, and weaken the ground over time.
actions: Slope the ground so water flows away from the walls
Clear blocked drains and channels
Add gutters and downpipes that empty away from the building
Check for leaking pipes
Add a concrete apron or paving around the base of the wall
standing_water.see_professional: If water enters the house, reaches the foundation, or the base of the wall is cracking or sinking, ask a registered engineer to inspect.
